==Problem==

The positive integers <math> x</math> and <math> y</math> are the two smallest positive integers for which the product of <math> 360</math> and <math> x</math> is a square and the product of <math> 360</math> and <math> y</math> is a cube. What is the sum of <math> x</math> and <math> y</math>?

<math> \textbf{(A)}\   80    \qquad
\textbf{(B)}\    85   \qquad
\textbf{(C)}\    115   \qquad
\textbf{(D)}\    165   \qquad
\textbf{(E)}\    610</math>

==Solution==
Take the prime factorization of <imath>360</imath>. <imath>360=2^3*3^2*5</imath>.
We want <imath>x</imath> to be as small as possible. And you want <imath>x*360</imath> to be a square.
So <imath>x=2*5=10</imath>.
<imath>y</imath> is similar. <imath>y=3*5^2=3*25=75</imath>
So, <imath>x+y=75+10=85</imath>, or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 85}</imath>.

~ModestFox97
